concepts.title: Direct Proportion
concepts.definition: Two quantities are in direct proportion when they grow or shrink by the same factor, keeping their ratio constant: more sugar costs more money in the same per-kilo way, so x1 over y1 equals x2 over y2 for any two corresponding pairs.
concepts.key_idea: Same factor everywhere: double one, the other doubles; the ratio x over y never moves.
question_patterns: if 5 kg of sugar costs 200 rupees what do 8 kg cost
a car travels the given distance in the given litres - find the distance for more litres
the cost of the pens is in direct proportion - find the missing value
which of the given pairs are in direct proportion
use the unitary method to complete the proportional table
find the cost of the bigger order from the smaller one

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the known output by the new input value.
Dividing by x1 keeps the constant ratio.

concepts.title: Inverse Proportion
concepts.definition: Two quantities are in inverse proportion when one rises by a factor while the other falls by the same factor, keeping their product constant: more workers finish a job in fewer days, since workers times days stays fixed.
concepts.key_idea: Product locked: x1 y1 equals x2 y2, so more of one means less of the other.
question_patterns: 6 workers finish a job in 12 days - how long do 9 workers take
a car moving at the given speed takes the given time - find the time at a new speed
which of the given pairs are in inverse proportion
the food stocked for the given days runs out earlier - how many people joined
find the missing value in the inverse proportion table
explain why speed and time are inversely proportional for a fixed journey

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the known pair for the constant.
The partner value is the constant over the new input.

concepts.title: Telling Direct and Inverse Apart
concepts.definition: The test is the factor behaviour: if doubling one quantity doubles the other they are directly proportional, but if doubling one halves the other they are inversely proportional; stories of buying point direct, stories of sharing work point inverse.
concepts.key_idea: Ask what doubling does: same direction means direct, opposite means inverse.
question_patterns: decide whether the given quantities are in direct or inverse proportion
are the number of workers and time in direct proportion - justify
what happens to the cost when the quantity doubles at the same rate
classify the given word problems as direct or inverse
give two daily life examples each of direct and inverse proportion
why is area of land and its cost in direct proportion

solution_steps.explain: Watch what the story forces on the other quantity.

solution_steps.action: check the ratio or the product
solution_steps.explain: Constant ratio means direct; constant product means inverse.

worked_examples.question_pattern: If {x1} kg of sugar costs {y1} rupees, what will {x2} kg cost?

solution_template.explain: The quotient is the new cost.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A machine prints {y1} pages in {x1} minutes. How many pages in {x2} minutes at the same rate?

solution_template.explain: Pages grow with minutes in direct proportion.
The quotient is the new page count.

worked_examples.question_pattern: {x1} workers finish a job in {y1} days. How many days will {x2} workers take?
A car covers the journey in {y1} hours at {x1} km/h. Find the time at {x2} km/h.

solution_template.explain: Speed times time is the fixed distance.
